# datocms_workflow (Resource)

Manages a DatoCMS workflow (UI: Settings > Workflows > "New workflow"). A workflow implements a state machine that lets content move through a series of custom approval stages, from draft to publication. Each stage is one entry of `stages`; the stage with `initial = true` is where new records enter the workflow.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Editorial workflow mirroring the "New workflow" screen of the DatoCMS UI
# (Settings > Workflows): content moves from writing to review, approval and
# publication. Exactly one stage must set initial = true; records enter the
# workflow at that stage.
resource "datocms_workflow" "approval_by_publisher" {
  # UI: "Name" and "API identifier".
  name    = "Approval by publisher"
  api_key = "approval_by_publisher"

  # UI: "Workflow stages" > "Add new stage". Each element is one stage, in
  # order; description is optional.
  stages = [
    {
      id          = "work_in_progress"
      name        = "Work in progress"
      description = "Content is being written"
      initial     = true
    },
    {
      id          = "in_review"
      name        = "In review"
      description = "Editor has finished writing and is waiting for approval"
    },
    {
      id   = "approved"
      name = "Approved"
    },
    {
      id   = "ready_to_publish"
      name = "Ready to publish"
    },
    {
      id          = "changes_requested"
      name        = "Changes requested"
      description = "The reviewer asked for changes before approval"
    },
  ]
}
```

## Mapping from the DatoCMS UI

The table below maps every field of the "New workflow" form in the DatoCMS UI (Settings > Workflows) to its Terraform attribute. Fields marked with `*` are required in the UI.

| UI field | Terraform attribute | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Name* | `name` | required |
| API identifier* | `api_key` | required |
| Workflow stages > Add new stage | `stages` (each stage is one list element with `id`, `name`, optional `description` and `initial`) | required, at least one |

Set `initial = true` on exactly one stage: that is the stage where new records enter the workflow.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_key` (String) Workflow API key: the machine-readable identifier used to reference the workflow through the API (for example from role item type permissions). UI: "API identifier".
- `name` (String) The name of the workflow. UI: "Name".
- `stages` (Attributes List) The ordered stages of the workflow (at least one). UI: "Workflow stages" > "Add new stage". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--stages))

### Optional

- `project` (String) Key of the provider's `api_tokens` map whose token is used for all API calls of this resource. When omitted, the default token (`api_token` attribute or `DATOCMS_API_TOKEN` environment variable) is used. Changing this attribute forces the resource to be recreated, since each key targets a different DatoCMS project.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Workflow identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--stages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `stages`

Required:

- `id` (String) Machine-readable identifier of the stage (for example `waiting_for_review`).
- `name` (String) Human-readable name of the stage.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Description of the stage's purpose.
- `initial` (Boolean) Whether this is the initial stage of the workflow. Set it to `true` on exactly one stage.

## Import

Import is supported using the workflow ID, optionally prefixed with the project key of the provider's `api_tokens` map (`project/id`):

```shell
# Workflows can be imported using the workflow ID
# (shown in the URL when editing the workflow in the DatoCMS UI, or returned by GET /workflows).
terraform import datocms_workflow.approval_by_publisher 949

# When the resource uses a project from the provider's api_tokens map,
# prefix the ID with the project key ("project/id").
terraform import datocms_workflow.approval_by_publisher store-one/949
```
